//: Pins for the code-signing TOOLS (never credentials - those come only from environment
variables, the certificate store, or CI secrets; see docs/developer-guide/releasing.md).
Both packages are fetched from nuget.org into tools/signing by Sign-Artifacts.ps1 and
verified against the SHA-512 that nuget.org itself publishes for the package (its
catalog 'packageHash'), NOT a hash of whatever happened to download. Nothing here is
installed system-wide and nothing here ships in the product.
To upgrade: pick a version on nuget.org, copy packageHash from
update the entry, and run build/Sign-Artifacts.ps1 -DryRun, then a real signing run.

artifactSigningClient.//: Azure Artifact Signing (formerly Trusted Signing). Only fetched when that method is used.

timestampServers.//: RFC 3161 servers, tried in order; each is retried before moving to the next. Plain http is normal for RFC 3161: the response is itself signed by the timestamp authority.

trustedThirdPartyPublishers.//: Signers whose EXISTING signatures on shipped third-party files are accepted as they are (the .NET runtime, WPF, and friends). Anything they did not sign, Captr signs itself. Matched against the signing certificate's common name.

ownFilePatterns.//: Files that must carry CAPTR's signature and no one else's: our own binaries, the bundled FFmpeg (signed by us after its pinned digest is verified), and the installer and uninstaller.
